units.title: Reciprocal polynomial roots forced close by six disk sectors
units.statement: For a degree-d polynomial with nonzero palindromic coefficients and simple roots, z is a root exactly when 1/z is. Hence at least N=ceil(d/2) distinct nonzero roots lie in the closed unit disk. Partition the disk into six half-open sectors of angle 60°. Two nonzero roots in the same sector have distance strictly less than 1. If N=6q+r with 0≤r<6, distributing roots as evenly as possible yields at least 6·q(q−1)/2+r·q close pairs. For d≥13 this is positive, proving the source result.
steps: Use P(z)=z^dP(1/z) to pair nonunit roots reciprocally
Place at least ceil(d/2) roots in the six sectors of the unit disk
Count same-sector pairs with a balanced occupancy argument
